Use case: historical-scene / production sprite animation. The supplied museum plate is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: Yi Am and Byeon Sang-byeok Joseon cats (16th and 18th centuries). Paint a NEW cat in this actual historical Korean ink-and-light-color animal-painting language: delicate short fur ink strokes, flat restrained washes, slightly angular elegant outlines, elongated flexible torso, small almond eyes, thin legs and natural head proportions. NOT modern cute watercolor, NOT western storybook, NOT plush, no huge round eyes or oversized head, no 3D shading. Small young cream-white Korean shorthaired kitten with a few pale ochre patches, small pointed face and slender legs, NOT a baby-faced plush toy. OUTPUT ONE SPRITE SHEET: EXACTLY 4 COLUMNS x 2 ROWS, 8 equally sized square cells; landscape 2:1 ratio. Same individual cat, same markings, SAME SCALE and head/body proportions in all cells. ALL face LEFT in three-quarter side view. TOP row four IDLE frames: standing alert, breathing, blinking, ear twitch. BOTTOM row four DISTINCT GALLOP/POUNCE frames for rushing toward fish: 1 crouched push-off hind legs loaded, 2 airborne full extension forelegs reach left hind legs stretch right, 3 forepaw contact hind legs tuck under, 4 recovery with back arched and legs gathered. Clear anatomical four-legged motion; no duplicate chase poses. Each entire cat including tail fits fully inside its OWN cell with at least 8 percent padding; no contact or overlap across cells, no ground lines, no dividers, no labels, no fish. Genuine transparent alpha outside every cat; remove the paper ground and all scenery. Fine dry-brush and subtle ochre only INSIDE silhouettes. Canvas suitable for equal grid slicing.

Use case: compositing / identity-preserve. Edit target is this existing Korean beauty cutout. Preserve exactly the same woman's pose, face, elaborate black hair, white jeogori with dark purple collar and blue skirt; keep full figure and all hands and clothing. Add a traditional Korean painted backdrop surrounding her to turn her into a complete rectangular miindo painting: pale warm hanji paper with faint distant ink mountains, restrained plum branch and a few low flowers. Same figure identity, no redesign, no perspective, straight-on portrait painting. Thin subtle ink outer edge. Background exists only inside a portrait rectangular sheet, transparent outside. No hanging hardware, frame, labels or calligraphy. The game swaps this in when the existing woman is pasted onto a wall.
